data.gender_notes: Ferozeht is used as a unisex name in Islamic naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: Derived from the Persian word 'Farrokhzad', meaning 'Victorious, Radiant, or Fortunate'. In Urdu, it is derived from 'Feroz', meaning 'Conqueror'. This name represents the beauty, strength, and triumph of its bearer. The name Ferozeht carries the meaning “Victorious, Radiant” and is chosen by families in Islamic traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Arabic tradition and is also used in Urdu, Persian. Parents who choose Ferozeht usually hope their child will grow to embody victorious, radiant and live with faith, good character and purpose.

historical_references.context: Ferozeht was a Persian princess who was known for her beauty and grace. She was the daughter of King Hormizd IV and was married to the Byzantine Emperor Justinian I. The marriage was a political one and was aimed at strengthening the relations between the Persian and Byzantine Empires. Ferozeht is remembered for her role in the transfer of the True Cross from Persia to Constantinople.
